channel.title: US Visa Policy (English)
channel.description: U.S. visa and immigration policy, fast and accurate

item.title: DHS Criticizes New York City for Releasing Previously Deported Noncitizen With Criminal Record
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 6, 2026, criticizing New York City officials for releasing Alonzo Reyes-Garcia, a Mexican national with prior convictions including robbery and assault, after ICE lodged a detainer on October 30. DHS says Reyes-Garcia was previously removed in 2006 under a final order of removal and later re-entered the country illegally. The release is the first in a new DHS series highlighting cases where local jurisdictions declined to honor ICE detainers.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Convicted Sex Offenders and Drug Traffickers
item.description: ICE reported the arrest of five individuals with prior criminal convictions, including child molestation, sexual assault and drug trafficking. The arrests occurred over one day across California, Texas, Virginia, Delaware and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

item.title: Secret Service Arrests Venezuelan Migrant with Guns Near White House, ICE Lodges Detainer
item.description: DHS said U.S. Secret Service officers arrested a Venezuelan national who is in the country illegally after finding multiple firearms and ammunition in his vehicle near the White House and after he said he intended to harm President Trump. ICE has lodged a detainer against him while he faces state firearms, theft and vehicle charges in Washington, D.C.

item.title: Five Cuban Nationals and Florida Man Sentenced in Smuggling, Asylum Fraud, Money Laundering Case
item.description: USCIS said it helped federal authorities secure prison sentences for five Cuban nationals and one U.S. citizen who ran an alien smuggling, ESTA fraud and asylum fraud operation that also laundered more than $22 million. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Florida announced the sentences, which followed guilty pleas by the defendants.

item.title: ICE Lodges Detainer for Peruvian National Arrested for Rape in New York City
item.description: DHS announced that ICE lodged a detainer on November 3, 2026 for a Peruvian national arrested by the New York Police Department in connection with an alleged rape. DHS said the individual had previously been apprehended by Border Patrol in 2023 and released into the country, and used the case to criticize New York's policies on cooperating with ICE, including a state law barring local police from partnering with the agency.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Illegal Aliens Convicted of Child Molestation, Assault, Drug Trafficking
item.description: ICE arrested five illegal aliens with criminal convictions including child molestation, sexual assault, and drug trafficking in several states. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the arrests reflect continued enforcement against public safety threats.

item.title: DHS Criticizes Minnesota County for Not Honoring ICE Detainer on Somali National With Prior Convictions
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 5, 2026 criticizing Hennepin County, Minnesota officials for not honoring an ICE detainer and releasing Mustafa Abdirahman Abdi, a Somali national with convictions including aggravated assault and drug trafficking. ICE had lodged the detainer on October 24, 2026, asking that Abdi not be released from jail, but the county released him anyway. DHS noted that Abdi received a final removal order in April 2021 but was released into the United States that same month under the previous administration.

item.title: DHS Highlights ICE Arrests of Criminal Immigrants on Election Day
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 4, 2026, highlighting ICE arrests made on Election Day, November 3, of individuals it describes as criminal illegal aliens with prior convictions including attempted murder, aggravated assault and child molestation. The release names five people arrested in Utah, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey and Minnesota.

item.title: DHS Touts Record Border Enforcement and Deportation Numbers Under Trump Administration
item.description: DHS issued a press release summarizing border enforcement and immigration removal statistics since President Trump returned to office. The release highlights border wall construction, arrest and deportation totals, and drug seizure figures as evidence of policy success.

item.title: DHS Criticizes Washington State Officials for Refusing ICE Detainer on Convicted Child Molester
item.description: DHS issued a statement criticizing sanctuary policies in Washington State after local authorities declined to honor an ICE detainer for a Venezuelan national convicted of child molestation. ICE said it lodged the detainer on October 14, asking to be notified before the individual's release from state custody.

item.title: DHS Announces ICE Arrests of Five Immigrants With Prior Criminal Convictions
item.description: DHS said ICE arrested five individuals described as criminal illegal aliens in North Carolina, Florida, California, Idaho and Texas, citing prior convictions including child-related offenses, assault and multiple DWIs. The release is part of a recurring DHS public safety campaign highlighting individual enforcement actions.

item.title: Canadian Lawful Permanent Resident Charged with Falsely Claiming US Citizenship to Vote
item.description: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri announced that Christopher Doucet, a Canadian-born lawful permanent resident, was indicted for falsely claiming U.S. citizenship on a voter registration form. The case was investigated by ICE Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS.

item.title: DHS Criticizes California Sanctuary Policies After Nearly 24,000 Criminal Immigrants Released From Jail
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security issued a statement criticizing California state and local officials for not honoring U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainers, saying this has led to the release of nearly 24,000 people with criminal histories who are in the country illegally since January 20, 2025. DHS says these individuals have more than 81,000 associated criminal charges or convictions, including homicide and sexual assault cases. The statement also cites specific recent criminal cases in California and other states.

item.title: DHS Announces Results of 'Operation Guardian' Crackdown on Illegal Aliens Holding Commercial Driver's Licenses
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced that Operation Guardian, a three-day enforcement operation conducted by ICE and state and local partners across 15 states from October 26 to 28, 2026, resulted in more than 230 arrests of illegal aliens, including over 40 holders of commercial driver's licenses (CDLs). The operation targeted unauthorized CDL holders and other public safety threats in the trucking industry.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Recent ICE Arrests of Alleged Criminal Aliens in Iowa
item.description: DHS issued a press release highlighting several individuals arrested by ICE in Iowa, citing their alleged criminal histories including burglary, domestic violence, drug trafficking and illegal reentry. The release is a public statement, not a new rule or policy change.

item.title: DHS Highlights ICE Arrests of Convicted Noncitizens in Kansas
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 2, 2026 describing five noncitizens arrested by ICE in Kansas between October 7 and October 28, 2026. The release lists each person's nationality, arrest location, and prior criminal convictions, including child sex offenses, aggravated battery, narcotics distribution and burglary.

item.title: ICE Reports Weekend Arrests of 15 Noncitizens with Serious Criminal Convictions
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested 15 noncitizens described as criminal illegal aliens over the weekend, citing convictions including manslaughter, child rape, child molestation, and armed robbery. The release lists each person's name, country of origin, conviction, and the jurisdiction where it occurred, and points to a DHS webpage with further cases.

item.title: 13 Brazilian, Cuban Nationals Federally Charged in Florida Visa and Marriage Fraud Scheme
item.description: The U.S. Attorney's Office in Orlando announced that 13 aliens from Brazil and Cuba have been indicted on charges including wire fraud, visa fraud, marriage fraud and unlawful employment of aliens. USCIS assisted the investigation, which found that a company called Legacy Imigra Solutions LLC falsely posed as an operation run by immigration experts and attorneys.

item.title: Visa Bulletin for November 2026: Family and Employment Dates Advance
item.description: The Department of State's November 2026 Visa Bulletin advances final action dates for most family-sponsored and employment-based immigrant visa categories compared to October 2026. Family preference F1, F2B, F3 and F4 categories move forward by about one year, while employment-based second preference advances 90 days for most countries. EB-1 and most EB-5 categories remain current for all countries except China and India.

item.title: ICE Lodges Detainer After Maryland Stabbing, Citing Earlier Release in New York
item.description: DHS said ICE lodged a detainer for Abubakarr Barrie, a Sierra Leonean national in the country illegally, after he was charged with attempted murder and kidnapping over the stabbing of a 15 year old girl in Baltimore on October 22, 2026. DHS said Barrie entered the United States illegally through Arizona in December 2023 and was later released, and that New York authorities did not honor an earlier ICE detainer after a July 2026 arrest.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Arrests of Serious Criminal Aliens in Florida
item.description: DHS issued a press release highlighting five illegal aliens recently arrested by ICE in Florida, citing criminal histories including vehicular homicide, sexual assault, domestic violence, arson, and robbery. The statement is a publicity release about specific enforcement cases and does not announce any new policy or rule.

item.title: DHS Announces ICE Arrests of Convicted Murderers, Rapists and Child Abusers
item.description: DHS issued a press release on October 30, 2026 stating that ICE arrested five illegal aliens nationwide with prior convictions including homicide, drug-induced rape and continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin framed the arrests as part of ongoing enforcement under President Trump.

item.title: DHS Says ICE Arrested Guatemalan National Earlier Released Under LA Sanctuary Policy
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested Guatemalan national Juan Jose Leonardo De Leon in Los Angeles on October 19, 2026. According to DHS, De Leon has prior convictions for drug offenses and grand theft, and had been released by local authorities in January 2026 after they declined to honor an ICE detainer. The release also lists numerous other cases in California and other states where DHS says sanctuary policies led to the release of noncitizens subject to ICE detainers.

item.title: ICE Reports Over 4,000 Arrests in Texas-Wide 'Lone Star Mission' Enforcement Operation
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced the results of a ten-day ICE enforcement operation across Texas called Lone Star Mission. ICE said the operation led to the arrest of 4,170 people without legal immigration status, including individuals with convictions for violent crimes.

item.title: DHS Says ICE Arrested Convicted Murderers, Sexual Predators and Drug Traffickers
item.description: DHS announced on October 29, 2026 that ICE arrested five illegal aliens with prior criminal convictions for crimes including murder, first-degree sexual assault, and drug trafficking. Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the arrests continue despite what DHS describes as a more than 1,600 percent increase in assaults against ICE officers.

item.title: USCIS Reports 2.2 Million Immigration Enforcement Actions Since January 2025
item.description: USCIS announced it has carried out approximately 2.2 million enforcement actions to revoke or terminate the immigration status of noncitizens since January 20, 2025. The agency says these actions include changes to Temporary Protected Status (TPS), denials of nonimmigrant status applications, issuance of Notices to Appear, an end to automatic EAD extensions, and termination of categorical parole programs.

item.title: State Department Imposes Visa Restrictions on Migrant Caravan Organizers
item.description: The U.S. Department of State says it will use an existing visa-restriction policy against individuals who organize, promote, support, or finance migrant caravans heading to the United States, as well as against caravan participants themselves. In the past week it imposed visa restrictions on more than 15 people tied to recent caravans moving through Central America and Mexico.

item.title: USCIS Reports 2.2 Million Enforcement Actions Since January 2025, Citing TPS, EAD, Parole Changes
item.description: DHS announced that USCIS has carried out approximately 2.2 million immigration enforcement actions revoking or terminating status since January 20, 2025. The agency says this figure is separate from State Department visa revocations and denials and ICE removals.

item.title: DHS Highlights Criminal Illegal Aliens Arrested by ICE in South Carolina
item.description: DHS published a press release naming five illegal aliens arrested by ICE in South Carolina, citing their criminal histories including voluntary manslaughter, assault, burglary, drug trafficking and hostage-taking. The release is a law enforcement publicity statement and does not announce any new policy or rule change.

item.title: DHS Updates Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act Entity List With Three New Companies
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security, as Chair of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force, published an updated UFLPA Entity List adding three companies linked to forced labor practices in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. This is a trade and import enforcement matter, not a visa or immigration policy change.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Illegal Aliens Convicted of Murder, Child Sex Assault, and Drug Trafficking
item.description: On October 28, 2026, ICE announced the arrest of five illegal aliens with prior convictions for crimes including murder, predatory sexual assault of a child, aggravated assault, and drug trafficking. The press release is part of ICE's ongoing publicity around enforcement actions against people it describes as criminal illegal aliens.

item.title: DHS Publicizes ICE Arrests of Texas Immigrants With Criminal Records
item.description: DHS issued a press release on October 28, 2026 highlighting five individuals arrested by ICE in Texas between September and October 2026, each with criminal convictions ranging from manslaughter and drug offenses to burglary and driving while intoxicated. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin credited cooperation between ICE and Texas state and local authorities for enabling the arrests. The release announces no new rule, fee, or deadline; it is intended to showcase ongoing enforcement actions.

item.title: ICE Arrests Dozens of Noncitizens in Nationwide Voter Fraud Crackdown
item.description: DHS said ICE arrested dozens of noncitizens across the country accused of illegally registering to vote or voting in U.S. elections. The release lists 13 example cases, several involving prior criminal convictions, and cites additional arrests, indictments and a conviction from March through October 2026 in multiple states. DHS said it directed ICE in June to apply stricter penalties, including deportation, to noncitizens who vote illegally.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Five ICE Arrests of Convicted Immigrants in Ohio
item.description: DHS issued a press release naming five people it calls illegal aliens arrested by ICE in Ohio in October 2026, citing criminal convictions including sexual assault, strangulation, DUI and cocaine trafficking. The release includes each individual's name, country of origin, arrest location and date, and listed criminal history.

item.title: DHS Criticizes New York Sanctuary Officials Over Release of Alien Charged in Officer Assault
item.description: DHS issued a statement condemning New York City officials for declining an ICE detainer and releasing Alpha Bah, an alien from Guinea charged with aggravated assault on a police officer with a deadly weapon. The release is a political statement about sanctuary policies, not a change to immigration law, rule or policy.

item.title: DHS Orders Exclusion and Removal of Acronis IT Products from Federal Civilian Agencies
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has filed a notice for publication stating that the Secretary of Homeland Security ordered the exclusion of Acronis AG and affiliated entities' information technology products from federal civilian executive branch procurements, and their removal from existing federal civilian IT systems. The action relies on authority under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act of 2018.

item.title: Suburban Chicago Man Sentenced for Staging Robberies to Enable U Visa Fraud
item.description: Parth Nayi, 29, of Woodridge, Illinois, was sentenced to two years in federal prison for organizing staged armed robberies between 2022 and 2024 so participants could fraudulently apply for U visas. USCIS assisted in the investigation, which was announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Illinois.

item.title: ICE Arrests Five Foreign Nationals With Convictions for Murder, Sexual Assault
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested five foreign nationals it described as having prior convictions for serious crimes, including first-degree murder, sexual abuse of children and sexual assault. DHS said the arrests are part of ongoing immigration enforcement targeting individuals with criminal records.

item.title: DHS Secretary Mullin Visits Coast Guard's Elite HITRON Helicopter Interdiction Squadron
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin toured the Coast Guard's Helicopter Interdiction Tactical Squadron (HITRON) in Jacksonville, Florida, observing demonstrations of airborne use-of-force tactics against drug trafficking vessels. The visit is a maritime drug interdiction showcase and has no direct bearing on visa or immigration policy.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Arrests of About 20 Illegal Aliens With Murder, Abuse and Gang Records in ICE Custody
item.description: On October 27, 2026, DHS released a statement highlighting roughly 20 individuals, described as illegal aliens, who are currently in ICE custody and have criminal records including homicide, robbery, child abuse and gang membership. The release includes names, countries of origin, alleged gang affiliations and prior convictions for each person. The statement also includes remarks from the DHS Secretary defending ICE's enforcement activities.
